characters.name: Coach Kreeton
characters.description: Born Unlucky: He has incredibly bad luck. The Bus Came Back: He makes appearances in Season 11, still played byKel Mitchelltoo! Child Hater: Despite being a junior high school teacher, he hates kids and frequently insults the students. Jerkass: He's unpleasant to everyone he meets, usually towards children. Karmic Butt-Monkey: He has a pretty terrible attitude especially around kids. This might justify the things that happen to him.

characters.name: Ms. Piddlin
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: Her assistant Julio is deathly afraid of her and constantly in a state of panic for a reason. Berserk Button: Disrespecting, derogating, or deriding peas in front of Ms. Piddlin is the last thing on Earth you want to do. Hair-Trigger Temper: She gets set off every time she feels no one appreciates her peas. The problem is that anything outside an absolute love for them can set her off with one pea lover getting thrashed because she gave himtoo manypeas. High-Pressure Emotion: Whenever Ms. Piddlin feels that her peas are being disrespected, steam will start pouring out of her neck before going off on her unfortunate victim. Marshmallow Hell: Ms. Piddlin had a tendency to do this to Julio and the students.

characters.name: H. Ross Perot
characters.description: Cool Old Guy: He's a very popular person for his age because of all the money he has. But he also shows to be a reliable guy to Earboy, as he's one of the few people who doesn't make fun of Earboy's ears, having big ears himself.

characters.name: Mark Cant/Superdude
characters.description: Clark Kenting:Exaggeratedwith Superdude's alter ego "Mark Cant" (note theMeaningful Name). As per the trope namer, he wore frumpy clothes, a bow tie, and large black glasses, only to remove them when he donned his Superdude costume. The trick, though, was that Mark would inevitably end up in a place—including a locked closet, a washing machine, a bank vault, or a bathroom—where he was literally theonly personwho could possibly turn into Superdude; to draw further attention to it, he often emerged triumphantly after changing mere seconds after Mark disappeared. Despite the extremely obvious clues, though,no one ever connected the dots. Meaningful Name: Mark Cant is unable to deal with evil as himself, but he can do it as Superdude. Weaksauce Weakness: Superdude has a super form of lactose intolerance: he loses his powers if dairy products even touch him. At least with Superman you can explain that his reaction to kryptonite is because it has a radioactive signature that heavily affects him, but Superdude doesn't even need to befedthe dairy product.

characters.name: Milkman
characters.description: Logical Weakness: He frequently disarmed of his various dairy products he uses to weaken Superdude due to other people outrighteatingsaid weapon. After all, things like cheese, milk, butter, and ice cream are practically harmless to folks who aren't lactose intolerant. Man of Kryptonite: Well sort of, but given he's likely an actual milkman he obviously has access to all the diary products he needs to try and defeat Superdude.

characters.name: The Sweaty Woman
characters.description: Orphaned Setup: In her first 2 appearances, it was explained that one of the Superdude's powers was the ability to make women endlessly perspire—at which point she would appear (now drenched) and yell "IT'S TRUE!" In later Superdude sketches, though, the superpower explanation was no longer included, making it seem like Denberg's character was sweating profusely for no particular reason (although it's possible that the producers just went with Nothing Is Funnier instead).

characters.name: Yo-Gurl
characters.description: Card-Carrying Villain: When Superdude asks why she's trying to fight him, she outright states that the only reason she has for it is that she thinks her (a villain made out of a dairy product) winning a fight against him (a lactose-intolerant superhero) would be natural. Logical Weakness: Cold temperatures. After all, there is such a thing as frozen yogurt. Scissors Cuts Rock: Despite being a more blantantMan of Kryptoniteagainst Superdude than Milkman, once Superdude gets enough breathing room to not be affected by her yogurt body he simply freezes her with his super chilled breath.

characters.name: The Fake Superdude
characters.description: Greed: This ends up being herFatal Flaw, because even though she was close to escaping with the stolen money, she insisted on taking aBank Toasterwith her, and when Superdude used his magnetic butt to pull it towards him, she engages in a tug-of-war with it rather than let go as she should've done. This gets her caught and arrested when she was so close to victory. Superdude even lampshades it.Superdude:You should've let go of the toaster, but youHADto be greedy, didn't you? Mundane Made Awesome: The only "superpower" she has is making ripping a piece of paper in half look awesome. Paper-Thin Disguise: Despite wearing an identical Superdude costume, she's still a little girl compared to the real deal, who is big and strong. Despite that, no one apart from him can tell the difference until she's revealed to not be lactose-intolerant. If she was, she might've had a chance. Spot the Imposter: Parodied when she needs to be identified from the real Superdude, because even though she looks way different than Superdude and is doing a terrible job at exhibiting real superpowers, the real Superdude is the only one who isn't falling for it.

characters.name: Coldfinger
characters.description: Expy: Of the titular villain ofGoldfinger.

characters.name: Captain Tantrum
characters.description: Improbable Age: Lampshaded in her debut sketch how she's just a child, including needing a booster seat for the captain's chair. While she's prone to outbursts, she's shown to be a reliable captain to the crew. Wounded Gazelle Gambit: How she beats Thumbtax in their first encounter. She cries so hard that Thumbtax willingly lowers her starship's shields just to get Tantrum to stop, leaving her wide open for Tantrum to order a heavy barrage.

characters.name: Ed
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: He makes appearances again in Season 11. Catchphrase: "Welcome to Good Burger, home of the Good Burger, can I take your order?" Literal-Minded: Most of his screw-ups stem from him taking the requests from customers and his coworkers too literally. If someone asks for a Good Burger with nothing on it, he'll give them a plain bun because the hamburger patty is "something".

characters.name: Baggin Saggin Barry
characters.description: Always Someone Better: His third and final appearance on the show (and only Season 2 appearance) has him encountering a girl named Baggin SagginMary. She ends up stealing all the attention from Barry, who falls into a state of depression which Clavis snaps him out of.He manages to become popular again by pullingAbraham Lincolnout of his pants and eventually falls in love with Mary, who he later marries and has 3 kids with. And the kids haveBag of Holdingpants just like their parents! Bag of Holding: His pants seem to have unlimited space, as literally, everything can fit in them, including living people from a baby toAbraham Lincoln!

characters.name: Ishboo
characters.description: Catchphrase: Nearly every explanation of his standard behavior (which is multiple times per episode) begin with "In my foreign land, it is only proper to..." Where the Hell Is Springfield?: We never learn where his foreign land is. Even the souvenir T-shirt he receives as a gift simply has the title of "foreign land".

characters.name: Mrs.Hushbaum/TheLoud Librarian
characters.description: Berserk Button: Any sort of noisemaking in the library—whether it's quietly whispering, wearing jangling accessories, or coughing—infuriates her. As she puts it, "IF YOU CAN'T BE SILENT, THEN I WILL BEVIOLENT!" The joke, of course, is thatshe herselfis incapable of being quiet. Black-and-White Insanity: Anyone who makes noise in the library is automatically a villain in her eyes—whether they're choking on a snack, sneezing, thanking her for helping, orasking about books. Calling Your Actions: Mrs. Hushbaum has a tendency to (loudly) announce whatever she's doing in a given moment. A few examples:I'M GONNA FRY UP SOME BACON!TIME TO TEST MY STRENGTH ON THIS CARNIVAL DEVICE!THIS ALARM MEANS THAT IT'S LUNCH TIME!I'M LABELING THE BOOKS!NOW I'M IN A REALITY THAT'S VIRTUAL!I LOVES CHEWIN' ME SOME ICE! Connected All Along: The final Loud Librarian sketch reveals that Mrs. Hushbaum is a friend of Miss Fingerly, the main teacher at Dullmont Junior High. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: Despite her violent temper and cluelessness about her own noisy behavior, Mrs. Hushbaum demonstrates remarkable competency in everything from karate to weightlifting to hibachi-style cooking to construction work.

characters.name: Detective Dan
characters.description: Clueless Detective: If he ever actually arrests someone, he arrests the victim while helping the obviously guilty criminal get off scot free. Legacy Character: He returned in Season 11, with Josh Server playing him as he did in the past, and Kate Godfrey joining in as his daughter, Detective Ann.

characters.name: Repairman
characters.description: Catchphrase:Repairman-man-man-man!

characters.name: Peter and Flem
characters.description: Right Way/Wrong Way Pair: Exaggerated. Peter is a normal boy who does things the correct way, while Flem is aWild Childwhose methods are not only wrong, but also completely insane.Narrator:After watching a fine program, Peter turns off his television with the remote control.Flem uses a brick.

characters.name: The Island Girls
characters.description: Cloudcuckoolander: Kiki, which isn't pleasing for Fran, since she keeps interfering with Fran's escape attempts. Milestone Celebration: Kiki marks 25 years stranded on the island with Fran in their Season 11 appearance. They also finally manage to get off the island. Red Oni, Blue Oni: Kiki is the hyperactive and dimwitted red oni, and Fran is the serious and well-organized blue oni. Throw the Dog a Bone: After spending 25 years trapped on an island with a girl who didn't want them to leave, Fran finally manages to escape the island, with Kiki following soon after. Unfortunately, they stranded a delivery boy and a DJ on the island in their place by stealing their jet skis.

characters.name: Ashley
characters.description: Berserk Button: Stupid questions.Being accused of mean behavior too. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Appears to be a sickeningly sweet little girl but has a major temper whenever she is asked idiotic questions (which is all the time). Catchphrase: "Thaaaaaat's ME!" In-studio audience members started saying this along with her in Season 4. It also became aBorrowed Catchphrasewhen other cast members started using it. Enraged by Idiocy:Everyquestion Ashley receives has aCaptain Obviousanswer. Whenever she finishes reading a letter,she goes from calm to screamingand may occasionally mock the writer. Gosh Dang It to Heck!: In the "Ask Ashley" segment, the titular character often peppers her rants with "stinkin'".

characters.name: Antoine
characters.description: Catchphrase: What it is.

characters.name: Lump Maroon
characters.description: Catchphrase: Jupiter! One-Word Vocabulary: He only ever says "Jupiter".

characters.name: Bradley the Big Ol' Baby
characters.description: Manchild: His name isn't Bradley the Big Ol' Baby for nothing.

characters.name: Billy Fuco
characters.description: NO INDOOR VOICE: He's either always shouting (especially when he says his name) or enthusiastically loud.

characters.name: Winder Wonders
characters.description: No Celebrities Were Harmed: To Summer Sanders, Olympic swimmer and host of Nickelodeon'sFigure It Out.

characters.name: Bridgett
characters.description: Catchphrase: "[verb] later!", usually in response to stuff Claudia says.

characters.name: Claudia
characters.description: Goth Girls Know Magic

characters.name: Buzz and Kaffy
characters.description: Catchphrase: "SUGAR AND COFFEE!"In Season 10, where episodes were filmed on location, they started yelling "LOWER THOSE ORBS!" In Season 10, where episodes were filmed on location, they started yelling "LOWER THOSE ORBS!" Klatchian Coffee/Sugar Causes Hyperactivity: The two get hopped up on sugar and coffee via two large dispensers from the ceiling, one filled with sugar and one with coffee, which Buzz and Kaffy pour into the mouths of themselves and their guests. NO INDOOR VOICE: They're always yelling. Trademark Favorite Food: Sugar and coffee, as per the show's name.

characters.name: Lisa and Oswald
characters.description: Muppet: Oswald is one of these. Rule of Three: Later seasons teach 3 vocabulary words.

characters.name: Zigfried
characters.description: Catchphrase: Expect to hear him yell "Kumquat!" and "Jerk" if he has issue with other drivers. Drives Like Crazy: He actively violates several road rules while on the road. Hypocrite: As mentioned above, he tends to get angry at other drivers if they get in his way, but he's clearly unfit to be a taxi driver given how heDrives Like Crazy.

characters.name: Randy Quench, Volunteer Firefighter
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: Although he means well, he always leaves a trail of destruction in his path and inevitably causes more harm than good. Slightly justified, as he apparently forgets to take his medication on a regular basis. Catchphrase: "Here comes me!" Heroic Wannabe: His heart is in the right place when it comes to his firefighting ambitions, but his brain and sanity are somewhere else entirely. Insistent Terminology: He always refers to himself by his full title, complete with a logo.

characters.name: Thelma Stump
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: She returned for a Season 11 sketch, where she met the cast ofZoey 101(and yes, that includesher actress. Catchphrase: "Bacon good". Never Mess with Granny: She isn't your average little old lady; there's a reason she works security forAll That, even if she can easily be bribed with bacon. Food as Bribe: Anyone can bribe their way past her if they have bacon on hand. Trademark Favorite Food: Bacon.

characters.name: Carlee and Marlee
characters.description: Alpha Bitch: The only clothing they'll respect is their own.Well... with one exception.

characters.name: Bucket Man
characters.description: Blessed with Suck: He has amazing superpowers, but can't use them well because the bucket of radioactive waste that gave him said powers is stuck to his head.

characters.name: Brad and Heather
characters.description: Kiss-Kiss-Slap: They spend most of their sketches acting all lovey-dovey as per the sketches' theme, but in the final seconds, something always happens that leads to Heather getting violent with Brad. The only exception was a sketch where they directed their anger at Cupid for being rude to them.

characters.name: The LAMOS
characters.description: Blessed with Suck: Dr. Laser, Mega Butt, the Barber, and the Sprinker have superpowers that don't serve any functional use for crimefighting. Then there's Old Man and the Toddler, who don't have any powers at all. Breast Expansion: Mega Butt's power is that she can inflate her butt like a balloon. Super Zeroes: Their powers are completely ineffective. In both of their sketches, the villains easily defeat them.

characters.name: Marie Kiddo
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: Her methods of tidying up involve destroying anything and everything that doesn’t spark joy… and anything else that her client doesn’t stop her from destroying. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She initially comes across as a helpful person assisting kids with organizing. However, it's eventually revealed she's anAx-Crazypsychopath who uses her job as an excuse to violently destroy anything that doesn't give the client immediate joy, up to and including the kid's family house. Catchphrase: "DESTROY!"

characters.name: Larry Van Halen
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: He's the only one who doesn't understand the rules, and almost always loses. The one time he wins, it isn't a good thing. Yank the Dog's Chain: He's forced to return to the show every time he loses. In the final sketch, he finally succeeds in winning the game after 27 failed attempts... but is still given a worse prize than his opponent. He doesn't mind though, because he thinks it means he can finally stop playing... until it's revealed that the winner is forced back into the show every 28 games.

characters.name: Brie
characters.description: Cosmetic Catastrophe: She has a bad habit of trying to do hair and makeup tutorials while still high on anesthetic after dental surgery. For example, dabbing eyeshadow all over her face under the belief that it's one big eyeball.

characters.name: The Island Boys
characters.description: Cloudcuckoolander: Wyatt, which isn't pleasing for Walter, since he keeps interfering with Walter's escape attempts. Distaff Counterpart: To the Island Girls in the original run ofAll That. In terms of appearance, Fran and Wyatt are the large ones, while Kiki and Walter are the skinny ones. In terms of personality and desire to leave the island, Fran and Walter are the reserved ones focused on escaping, while Kiki and Wyatt are the hyperactive ones who don't want to go. Red Oni, Blue Oni: Wyatt is the hyperactive and dimwitted red oni, and Walter is the serious and well-organized blue oni.
